**User:** I want to jump back into the volleyball Excel workbook project that we were working on the other day. Do you recall this conversation? We made some adjustments to how Power Query pulled in data when Mike Weger was trying to access the file using his machine.

**Assistant:** I don't have that session in memory, so I'll search for it.

**Assistant:** The branch has been merged since then (PR #1), so that STATUS item is out of date. I'll check whether Box Drive is working now and whether the fixed file landed.

**Assistant:** Yes, I found it. It's the **Volleyball_GRID** project, and the last session was on 9/30. (One small thing: his name is spelled Mike **Wenger**.)

**What we fixed**
- **The problem:** Mike couldn't refresh the workbook. Box Drive opens the file in Excel as a web link, not as a `C:\` file path. Because of that, the cell that tells Power Query where to find the raw Kinexon data folder (Ref!D2) was always blank, for everyone. It only worked for you because there was a backup path hardcoded to your username.
- **The fix:** D2 now builds the path from whoever has the file open, `C:\Users\<name>\Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`. If no export in a folder can be read, the workbook skips that folder. If nothing works at all, it shows a clear error. Privacy levels are set to ignore, since every source is a local folder.
- **Testing:** It passed on your laptop using copies, including a run that pretended to be Mike. It has **not** been tested on Mike's laptop.

**Where things stand today**
- The fix is merged to main (PR #1). STATUS.md still says it isn't, so I'll update that.
- Box Drive is running again: Box and `streem` both started at 8:56 this morning, so the crash from 9/30 seems to be cleared.
- `Box\Kinexon\SandBox\VB_Revised_.xlsx` is in your Box folder, but it shows no size. That usually means Box hasn't downloaded it to the laptop yet. So I still can't confirm it's the fixed version, which should be 5,581,455 bytes and show a `C:\Users\...` path in Ref!D2.

**Next steps**
1. Open `VB_Revised_.xlsx` from Box. That makes Box download it. Then I'll check the size and Ref!D2.
2. Send Mike `docs/mike-refresh-checklist.md`. He refreshes once and tells you what Ref!D2 shows.

Do you want to open the file now so I can check it? Or was there something new you wanted to work on in the workbook?

**User:** [Image: source: C:\Users\eric_rash\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV\910615e7-bef8-4385-a3c4-7c4676114610\images\1.png]

On 9/30 we set the workbook to ignore privacy levels so this check wouldn't run. Since it's back, I'll check whether that setting actually survived in the file you're refreshing.

**Assistant:** The Box file was saved at 9:08 this morning and is 78 bytes bigger than the fixed copy, so it's essentially the fixed workbook. Next I'll compare the Power Query settings stored inside each file.

**Assistant:** Python can't open the Box copy directly, probably because Excel has it open. I'll copy it to a scratch folder and read the copy.

**Assistant:** The file was there a minute ago and now isn't. Excel may be in the middle of a save, or the file was renamed. I'll look at the folder again.

**Assistant:** Someone renamed it to `VB_Revised.xlsx` (no underscore) at 9:10. Reading that file now.

**Assistant:** I found the cause, and it's fixable.

**What happened:** The query code in the Box file is identical to our 9/30 fix. What changed is the workbook's "Ignore privacy levels" setting: it's switched back off in the Box file, though our fixed copy has it on. That setting was the only thing keeping this error from happening, so it's back. It most likely got reset when the file was saved at 9:08 or renamed at 9:10 (`VB_Revised_.xlsx` became `VB_Revised.xlsx`).

**To get yourself working right now (about 30 seconds):**
In Excel, go to Data → Get Data → Query Options → **Current Workbook → Privacy** → choose **"Ignore the Privacy Levels"**, click OK, then save and Refresh All. While you have that window open, also look at **Global → Privacy**. If it says "Always combine data according to your Privacy Level settings for each source," that overrides the per-workbook switch, so tell me what it says.

**That's only a band-aid.** If something can switch that setting off once, it can do it again, and Mike's own Excel settings can override it on his laptop. The real fix is to merge the five Power Query queries into one. The error comes from one query using results from another query while also reading a data source. With a single query, that can't happen. I'll test it on a copy with the privacy check switched **on**, so it proves the fix works without the band-aid. I won't touch the live Box file, and Mike doesn't get the checklist until that test passes.

Two quick questions before I build it:
1. **How did you open the file this morning?** From the Box folder in File Explorer, or from the Box website ("Open in Excel" / Excel Online)? Mike will open it the same way, and the web route may be what reset the setting.
2. **Did you rename it to `VB_Revised.xlsx` (no underscore)?** The docs and Mike's checklist still use the underscore name, so I'll update them to match.

**User:** That setting chaged didnt trigger the error on the refresh. I opened the file from Box folder, yes I renamed it — build the fix

**Assistant:** I'll check one thing first. If your Excel's global privacy option is set to "always ignore," a test on this laptop would pass even if the fix doesn't work.

**Assistant:** Now the baseline test: the current Box file with the privacy check on. It should reproduce your error, which proves the test can catch the bug.

**Assistant:** Baseline fails as expected. Now the fixed version, also with the privacy check on:

**Assistant:** Both tests pass. Now I'll build the version to ship. It also keeps "ignore privacy levels" on as a backup, but the fix no longer depends on it. Then I'll confirm what got saved.

**Assistant:** The workbook is saved. It now has a single query, "ignore privacy levels" is on as a backup, and it's 5,764,598 bytes. Next I'll update the docs.

**Assistant:** Making the doc edits:

**Assistant:** Now STATUS.md:

**Assistant:** Everything's updated. I'll commit it on a branch and push, following the project's session routine.

**Assistant:** The fix is built and tested. Your error no longer occurs even when "ignore privacy levels" is switched off. The fixed file is **not in Box yet**; you upload it.

- The error came from **Kinexon Master** reading the raw data and also borrowing results from four small helper queries (Sample File, Transform File, Parameter1, Transform Sample File). - "Ignore privacy levels" is still switched on in the new file as a backup, but refresh no longer depends on it.

**Context:** Resumed the Volleyball_GRID Excel workbook project (last touched 9/30) to fix a Power Query refresh failure in `VB_Revised.xlsx` for Mike Wenger.

**Key Exchanges:**
- Eric hit the Power Query "Formula.Firewall" privacy error on Refresh All. Diagnosis: the Box copy had identical query code to the 9/30 fix, but the workbook-level "Ignore privacy levels" setting had been flipped back off — likely during the 9:08 save or the 9:10 rename of `VB_Revised_.xlsx` → `VB_Revised.xlsx`.
- Band-aid given (Data → Get Data → Query Options → Current Workbook → Privacy → Ignore). Eric confirmed toggling it stopped the error, that he opens the file from the Box folder in File Explorer, and that he did the rename. He said: build the real fix.
- Root cause of the firewall trip: `Kinexon Master` both read the raw-data folder and consumed results from four helper queries (Sample File, Transform File, Parameter1, Transform Sample File).

**Decisions Made:**
- Replaced the five-query structure with a **single self-contained `Kinexon Master` query**; deleted the four helper queries. With one query there is nothing for the firewall to block, so the fix no longer depends on the privacy setting. "Ignore privacy levels" left on as belt-and-suspenders only.
- Tested with privacy checks **on** (not bypassed), including a baseline that reproduced the error, proving the test can catch the bug.
- Don't touch the live Box file; Eric uploads. Mike's checklist is not sent until the fix is verified in Box.
- Checklist/docs updated to the new filename without the trailing underscore.

- A per-workbook "Ignore privacy levels" setting is not durable — saves, renames, and web-route opens can reset it, and a user's Global privacy setting can override it anyway. Structural fixes (collapse to one query) beat settings-based workarounds for files shared across machines.
- Verify tests aren't passing for the wrong reason: checked Eric's *global* Excel privacy option first, since "always ignore" would have made any test pass vacuously.
- Box Drive quirks: a 0-byte file usually means Box hasn't downloaded it locally yet; Python can't open a workbook Excel has open (copy to scratch first).

entries.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
entries.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, or `developer`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

objective.description: Optional broader goal for this search, if known. Avoid sensitive information.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation. `developer` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`; the other categories also filter `data.web`.
